# Ballsy

Turns a real football match into a short vertical recap video narrated by
Ballsy, an animated cartoon-ball mascot. See `README.md` for setup/usage.

## Core principle

**The video is composed with code, not generated by AI.** AI is used in
exactly two places: an LLM (Anthropic) writes the commentary script, and a
TTS model (ElevenLabs) voices it. Everything else — lip-sync, expressions,
event graphics, captions, mascot movement — is deterministic React/Remotion
rendering driven by real match data (SofaScore) and the exact script text.
Never suggest generative video/image models as a shortcut for any of this.

The script-writing agent is instructed to act as a **commentator, not a data
narrator** — it decides what's worth telling (skips a routine 20th-minute
yellow card, mentions one after a brawl) rather than listing every event.
Preserve that framing if touching `scripts/generate-script.mjs`'s prompt.

## Legal constraints (drove several design decisions — don't undo them)

- No real player faces, likenesses, or broadcast footage. Every graphic is
  generic: the ball, a scoreboard, a card, a substitution arrow.
- The mascot stays stylised/cartoonish on purpose, not a realistic avatar.
- Controversy commentary is always framed as opinion, never a factual claim
  about a real person.

## Pipeline (in order)

```
Pick a match (SofaScore)
  → generate-script.mjs      (Anthropic, paid)  → human review/edit/approve
  → generate-audio.mjs       (ElevenLabs, paid)  → audio + per-character alignment
  → generate-visemes.mjs     (Rhubarb, local)    → mouth-shape timeline
  → generate-expressions.mjs (local)             → expression timeline
  → generate-graphics-timeline.mjs (local)       → on-screen event graphics timeline
  → generate-avatar-timeline.mjs   (local)        → mascot position/scale keyframes
  → generate-captions.mjs    (local)             → word-level captions
  → Remotion render                              → final .mp4
```

Everything after the script is derived from the same two sources: the exact
script text (captions/timing) and SofaScore's structured match data (which
graphic, when, with which score/players). Nothing is transcribed or guessed
after the fact — if you add a new per-event graphic or script field, wire it
through this same chain rather than inventing a parallel data path.

## Key files

- `src/ballsy.tsx` — the mascot: drives the Rive state machine per-frame
  (`viseme` 0-8, `expression` 0-4), never lets Rive run its own clock.
  Renderer is created once and reused (don't call `makeRenderer()` per
  frame — it leaks). Avatar div renders *after* the graphics `<Sequence>`s
  so Ballsy sits in front of them.
- `src/graphics/*.tsx` — one component per event type (goal, card, penalty,
  substitution, clear chance, VAR review, goal disallowed). Shared tokens
  (`COLORS`, `Banner`, `Scoreboard`, `TitlePill`) live in `graphics/shared.tsx`.
- `scripts/sofascore/sofascore.py` — the only thing that talks to SofaScore
  (Cloudflare-bypassed via `curl_cffi` Chrome impersonation). Node calls it
  through `scripts/lib/match-source.mjs`, never directly.
- `scripts/generate-graphics-timeline.mjs` — matches script-tagged events to
  real SofaScore events for props (score, card colour, etc.), times each
  graphic to when its line is actually spoken (not the start of the
  sentence), and splits overlapping event windows (e.g. VAR review + the
  card it produces) sequentially instead of stacking them.
- `scripts/server/` — **Ballsy Studio**, the local web app (`npm run
  selector`, port 4321). Express backend (`index.mjs`) + a small
  no-framework TypeScript frontend (`src/app.ts`, compiled to
  `public/app.js` by its own `tsconfig.json` — the root `tsconfig.json`
  excludes `scripts/` on purpose, don't remove that). Has its own
  History-API router (`/`, `/history`, `/match/:id`).

## Gotchas

- Render final videos with `--concurrency=1` (`npm run selector`'s render
  step already does this). Remotion's default parallel rendering can make
  the mascot's stateful idle animation stutter at process seams.
- The Rive artboard background must stay transparent (no background
  rectangle) so Ballsy composites over the pitch background/graphics.
- SofaScore's VAR `confirmed` field: `true` = the labeled decision stood;
  `false` = it was overturned (the opposite happened). Getting this backwards
  makes the script narrate overturned calls as if they were final — see
  `VAR_REVIEW SEMANTICS` in `generate-script.mjs`'s prompt.
- ElevenLabs free tier: shared/professional Voice Library voices return 402;
  a custom Voice Design voice works. Paid plans aren't affected.
- Match ids are SofaScore event ids, used to build file paths
  (`scripts/output/<id>.json`, `public/audio/<id>*`, `out/<id>.mp4`) —
  always validate as numeric before interpolating into a path.

## Commands

```bash
npm run selector                    # Ballsy Studio (recommended entry point)
npx remotion studio                 # preview the current FIXTURE_ID live
npx tsc --noEmit                    # type-check src/
npx tsc -p scripts/server/tsconfig.json   # type-check + build the selector frontend
npx eslint src
```
